roots.cause.v: Two mechanisms, stated as found (no re-run). (1) Plus: the root SQL text is the same cache replay in both runs; a statement that finished in the fixed run's evaluation exceeded the execution time limit in the gated run's evaluation (status timeout); the gated loop treats a timeout as a failing root and revises, the fixed loop saw a result. Plus: gated 23 vs fixed 18 failing roots, 5 items differ, 5 of them with identical SQL; execution time depends on machine load, so this part is not reproducible to the item. (2) Flash and 27b: the gated run issued live generation requests whose request keys are absent from the fixed run (the prompt of the root request was not identical to the fixed run's; why it differed is not determined by the stored fields, a candidate is non-deterministic rerank output), so the root SQL was regenerated and differs in some items. cost.embed_rerank_included.v: No. Embedding and rerank requests per question are the counts recorded in preds.jsonl (embed_req, rerank_req); they count live HTTP requests only (a vector served from the local embedding cache is not counted), so the embedding count differs between arms for reasons unrelated to the method and is a lower bound of what a cold run issues; they are not priced in cny_q because (i) their per-token prices in exp/prices.yaml are unverified placeholders and (ii) the tokens of these requests are not recorded per item (usage rows exist only for live requests). cny_emb_placeholder is therefore not computable (n/a).

rev.def.v: Population: fixed loop (plus), 1,534 dev items; an item enters if the root candidate executes (status ok_nonempty or ok_empty) and the final SQL text differs from the root SQL text (strip-equal). helped = root EX 0 and final EX 1; hurt = root EX 1 and final EX 0; neutral = same EX. EX is execution accuracy against the original BIRD dev reference query. Repair of a non-executing root is counted separately. The annotation labels do not enter the counts.

rev.annotation_in_counts.v: no: the counts above are execution-based (EX against the original reference); annotation labels (rev.label.*) are attached afterwards for the items that happen to be in the annotated failure sample
